name: @projexlight/sdk-principal-token
summary: P10/E2 platform principal token — the trust primitive for delegated auth between the gateway and downstream services. The api-gateway mints a signed (HS256), audience-bound, short-TTL JWT from the SERVER-RESOLVED IdentityContext (mintPrincipalToken); claims derive only from resolved context, never from request input, which closes the confused-deputy class. Downstream services verify iss/aud/exp and signature (verifyPrincipalToken) via a Fastify preHandler (requirePrincipalToken) that also strips spoofable forwarded identity headers (x-user-id, x-tenant-id, ...) so identity is trusted ONLY from the verified token. Signing keys rotate (rotateSigningKey / startPrincipalKeyRotation), are stored AES-256-GCM wrapped at rest by a vault-sourced wrap key, and honor a retire_after overlap window so rotation never invalidates in-flight short-TTL tokens.

models.description: Rotating HS256 signing keys. One row per key (kid UUID PK) holding the AES-256-GCM secret_wrapped (base64(iv).base64(tag).base64(ct)), a status of active|retiring|retired, and a retire_after overlap instant. A partial unique index enforces at most one active key; retiring keys still verify until retire_after passes.

scenarios.title: Mint a scoped, audience-bound principal token at the gateway
scenarios.when_to_use: In the api-gateway, after resolving the caller's IdentityContext, when forwarding a request to a downstream service that must trust the caller's identity without re-resolving it. The token binds to a single target service (aud) and is short-lived.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Returns a signed HS256 JWT whose claims (sub/app_id/tenant_id/scopes/roles/personas) come only from the resolved principal, with aud='sdk-orders' and an exp capped at MAX_PRINCIPAL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS. The token is signed by the current active signing key and carries its kid header.

scenarios.title: Verify a presented principal token in a downstream service
scenarios.when_to_use: In any downstream service (or Fastify route) that receives a gateway-minted token and must establish trusted identity while rejecting spoofable forwarded identity headers.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Forwarded identity headers (x-user-id, x-tenant-id, ...) are deleted, the token from x-principal-token or Authorization: Bearer is verified for iss/aud/exp/signature, and req.principal is set to the verified claims. A missing token yields 401 PrincipalTokenRequired; an invalid/wrong-audience token yields 401 InvalidPrincipalToken.

scenarios.title: Rotate the signing key without invalidating in-flight tokens
scenarios.when_to_use: On a scheduled cadence, or immediately on suspected key compromise, to roll the HS256 signing key while tokens already minted under the old key stay verifiable until they expire.
scenarios.expected_outcome: The current active key transitions to 'retiring' with retire_after = now() + MAX_PRINCIPAL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS and a fresh active key is minted. verifyPrincipalToken tries the header-kid key first but still accepts retiring keys inside the overlap window, so in-flight short-TTL tokens keep verifying. onRotate fires with the new kid for audit.

compliance_posture.notes: Bearer-token trust primitive for service-to-service auth. Signing secrets are NEVER persisted in plaintext — they are AES-256-GCM wrapped by a vault-sourced wrap key (PRINCIPAL_TOKEN_WRAP_KEY or a wired vault provider), and production boot fails closed if no real wrap key is present. Tokens are least-privilege: audience-bound to a single service and short-TTL (default 300s, hard-capped at MAX_PRINCIPAL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS) to bound blast radius. Claims are minted solely from server-resolved identity, never request input, and downstream verification strips spoofable forwarded identity headers — closing the confused-deputy class. Key rotation with a retire_after overlap window supports periodic re-keying and emergency revocation on compromise via onRotate/rotateNow audit hooks.
